Muqatil said: admonish the disbelievers of Makkah, for the reminder benefits whoever, in God's knowledge, will believe.

It was said: remind them of the punishment and the Days of God. He specified the believers for reminding because they are the ones who benefit from it.

The clause ﴿And I did not create the jinn and humankind except to worship Me﴾ is a resumed clause confirming what precedes it, because the fact that their creation was for the mere purpose of worship is something that energizes the Messenger of God (ﷺ) for reminding, and energizes them to respond.

It was said: this is specific to those who, in God's knowledge, will worship Him; it is a general statement intended in a specific sense.

Al-Wahidi said: the exegetes said: this is specific to the people of His obedience, meaning those among both groups who are qualified.

He said: this is the saying of al-Kalbi, al-Dahhak, and the preference of al-Farra' and Ibn Qutayba.

Al-Qushayri said: the verse has definitely entered into specification, because the insane were not commanded to worship, nor did He intend it from them, and He has said: ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and humankind﴾ [al-A'raf: 179], and whoever is created for Hell is not among those created for worship.

So the verse is to be understood as referring to the believers among them, and this is indicated by the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "And I did not create the jinn and humankind among the believers except to worship Me."

Mujahid said: the meaning is: except that they may know Me.

Al-Tha'labi said: this is a fine saying, because if He had not created them, His existence and oneness would not have been known.

It is narrated from Mujahid that he said: the meaning is: except that I might command them and forbid them. This is indicated by His saying: ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship one God; there is no deity but Him; exalted is He above what they associate﴾ [al-Tawba: 31]. al-Zajjaj preferred this.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: it is what they were disposed to of happiness and wretchedness; so He created the happy among the jinn and humankind for worship, and created the wretched for disobedience.

Al-Kalbi said: the meaning is: except that they may declare Me one; as for the believer, he declares Him one in hardship and ease; as for the disbeliever, he declares Him one in hardship but not in blessing, as in His saying: ﴿And when a wave covers them like shadows, they call upon God, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Luqman: 32]. 

A group said: except that they may submit to Me and humble themselves. The meaning of worship in the language is: humiliation, submission and compliance. Every created being of humankind and jinn is subject to God's decree, humbled to His will, and compliant with what He has determined for him.

He created them as He willed, and provided for them as He decreed. None of them possesses for himself any benefit or harm.

The reason for mentioning the jinn before humankind here is the precedence of their existence.

﴿I do not want from them any provision, nor do I want them to feed Me.﴾ This sentence contains a clarification of His, glorified is He, independence from His servants, and that He does not want from them any benefit, as masters want from their slaves; rather He is the absolutely Rich, the Provider, the Giver.

It was said the meaning is: I do not want from them that they provide for anyone of My creation, nor that they provide for themselves, nor that they feed anyone of My creation nor feed themselves. He attributed feeding to Himself because all creation are God's dependents; whoever feeds God's dependents is as if he fed Him.

This is like what came in the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "God says: My servant, I asked you for food and you did not feed Me." That is, you did not feed My servants. And "min" in His saying "min rizq" (of provision) is extra, for the emphasis of generality.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 51, verse 38–60 (part 2 of 2):

Then the Exalted showed that He alone is the Provider (al-Razzaq), and none other. He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Provider, Possessor of power, the Firm.﴾ There is no provider besides Him and no giver other than Him. He is the One who provides for His creatures and takes care of what sustains them, so that they should not busy themselves with other than that for which they were created, namely worship. ﴿Possessor of power, the Firm﴾: the nominative (al-raf') of al-matin (the Firm) may be as an attribute of al-Razzaq, or of "dhu" (Possessor), or as the predicate of an omitted subject, or as a second predicate.

The majority of readers recite al-Razzaq. Ibn Muhaysin read al-Raziq. The majority read al-matin in the nominative. Yahya ibn Wathhab and al-A'mash read it in the genitive (al-jarr), as an attribute of al-quwwah (power). The masculine form is used because its feminine is not a true feminine.

Al-Farra' said: its correct form would have been al-matinah (feminine), but he made it masculine because he had in mind "the thing that is firm, well-twisted." One says a rope is matin, meaning well-twisted. The meaning of al-matin here is: intensely strong.

﴿Indeed, for those who have done wrong is a share (dhanub) like the share of their companions﴾: that is, they wronged themselves by disbelief and sins, so for them is a share (dhanub), i.e., a portion of punishment, like the portion of the disbelievers of the previous nations. Ibn al-A'rabi said: one says "a day of dhanub," meaning a day of long evil that does not end. The original meaning of dhanub in the language is a large bucket. Among the uses of dhanub for a portion of something is the poet's saying:

"By your life, and the fates are coming upon all the sons of one father, each has a dhanub of them."

What is in the verse is taken from the sharing of water-carriers by the large bucket, so it is a metaphor, in which dhanub is put in place of share and portion, as Ibn Qutaybah said. ﴿So let them not seek to hasten Me﴾: that is, let them not ask Me to hasten the punishment for them, as in their saying: ﴿Bring us what you promise us, if you are among the truthful.﴾

﴿So woe to those who disbelieved from their day which they are promised.﴾ It has been said that it is the Day of Resurrection, and it has been said that it is the Day of Badr. The fa' (so) indicates the sequence of what follows upon what precedes.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted, regarding His saying ﴿but he turned away with his pillar﴾, from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "with his people."

al-Firyabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, transmitted from him regarding His saying ﴿the barren wind﴾ that he said: "the violent one which does not fertilize anything."

Ibn Jarir also transmitted from him, that he said: "it does not fertilize trees nor stir up clouds." And regarding His saying ﴿but it left it like rotted debris﴾ he said: "like a thing that has perished."

al-Firyabi and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib that he said: "The barren wind is the nakba'" (a wind blowing from an unusual direction).

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying ﴿And the heaven We built with hands﴾ that he said: "with power."

Abu Dawud in his al-Nasikh and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from him regarding His saying ﴿So turn away from them, for you are not blameworthy﴾ that he said: "Allah commanded him to turn away from them in order to punish them, and excused Muhammad (ﷺ). Then He said: ﴿And remind, for the reminder benefits the believers﴾, and this abrogated it."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from him regarding His saying ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾ that he said: "to acknowledge servitude, willingly or unwillingly."

Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from him regarding the verse, that he said: "upon what I created them upon of obedience to Me and disobedience, of misery and happiness."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat transmitted from him also regarding His saying: "al-Matin" says: "the strong."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from him also regarding His saying: "dhanuban" he said: "a bucket."

His saying: "And in Musa" is conjoined to his saying "in it" (fihā) with the repetition of the preposition, and the implied meaning is: "And We left in the story of Musa a sign." Or it is conjoined to "and in the earth," and the implied meaning is: "And in the earth and in Musa are signs." This is what al-Farra', Ibn 'Atiyya and al-Zamakhshari said.

Abu Hayyan said: "This is very far-fetched; the Qur'an is too exalted for the like of it." It is also permissible that it be connected to a presumed "We made" (ja'alna), which is indicated by "We left" (taraknā). It was said: it is also permissible that it be conjoined to "We left" in the manner of the saying of the poet:

"I fed them chaff and cold water,"

and the implied meaning is: "We left in it a sign, and We placed in Musa a sign."

Abu Hayyan said: "There is no need to presume 'We placed,' because it is possible that the governing element of the genitive (majrur) is 'We left.'"

The first mode is the preferable one, and whatever else there is, is forced and strained; no need compels to it, and no necessity calls for it.

﴿When We sent him to Fir'awn with a manifest authority.﴾ The adverbial phrase (al-zarf) is connected to an omitted element which is the qualifier (na't) of the sign: that is, existing at the time We sent him; or it is connected to the sign itself. The first is preferable.

The manifest authority (al-sultan al-mubin) is the clear, evident proof, and it is the staff and what accompanied it of signs.

﴿But he turned away with his rukn.﴾ Al-tawalli is turning away (al-i'rad), and al-rukn is the side. This was said by al-Akhfash.

The meaning is: he turned away with his side, as in His saying: ﴿He turned away and withdrew with his side﴾ [al-Isra': 83]. Al-Jawhari said: the rukn of a thing is its strongest side, and "he takes refuge in a firm rukn" means: in might and protection.

Ibn Zayd, Mujahid and others said: the rukn is his army and his soldiers by whom he strengthened himself. From it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or I would take refuge in a firm rukn﴾ [Hud: 80], that is: a clan and protection. It was also said: the rukn is strength itself, and Qatada and others said this. From it is the saying of 'Antara:

"The rigors of war have not weakened my rukn,
but rather what has passed of my time."

﴿And he said: a sorcerer or a madman.﴾ That is, Fir'awn said concerning Musa: "He is a sorcerer or a madman." He vacillated, in regard to what he saw of Musa's conditions, between his being a sorcerer or a madman. This from the accursed one is a sophistry and a deception to his people, for he knows that what he saw of the marvels cannot be easily accomplished at the hand of a sorcerer, nor does one who is mad do such things.

It was said: "or" (aw) here has the meaning of "and" (wa), because he said all of that together and did not vacillate. This was said by al-Mu'arrij and al-Farra', like His saying: ﴿And do not obey from among them a sinner or a disbeliever﴾ [al-Insan: 24].

﴿So We seized him and his soldiers, and We cast them into the sea.﴾ That is, We threw them into the sea. The clause ﴿and he was blameworthy﴾ is in the place of an accusative as a circumstantial state (hal): that is, one who came with what he deserves to be blamed for, when he claimed lordship, disbelieved in God, and transgressed in his disobedience.

﴿And in 'Ad﴾: that is, and We left in the story of 'Ad a sign ﴿when We sent upon them the barren wind﴾, which is the one in which there is no good nor blessing, which does not fertilize trees nor bring rain; it is only a wind of destruction and punishment.

Then He, glorified is He, described this wind, saying: ﴿It left nothing it passed over but made it like the crumbled﴾. That is: it left nothing that passed over them, of their persons, their livestock and their wealth, but made it like a thing destroyed and decayed.

The poet said:

"Time left me when it withdrew from my sight,
and I remained like the decayed bone of the rimma."

Qatada said: it is what is trampled of dry vegetation. Al-Suddi and Abu al-'Aliya said: it is pulverized dust. Qutrub said: it is ash. The root of the word is from "ramma al-'azm": when a bone decays, it becomes rameem (crumbled). And al-rimma is decayed bones.

﴿And in Thamud, when it was said to them: enjoy yourselves until a time.﴾ That is, and We left in the story of Thamud a sign at the time We said to them: live enjoying the world until the time of destruction, which was three days, as in His saying: ﴿Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days﴾ [Hud: 65].

﴿But they defied the command of their Lord﴾: that is, they became arrogant regarding obedience to God's command. ﴿So the thunderbolt seized them﴾, and it is every destroying punishment.

The majority read al-sa'iqa (the thunderbolt). 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, Humayd, Ibn Muhaysin, Mujahid and al-Kisa'i read al-sa'qa. The discussion of al-sa'iqa has passed in al-Baqara and in other places. ﴿While they were looking﴾: that is, they were seeing it with their own eyes. The clause is in the place of an accusative as a circumstantial state. It was said that the meaning is: they were waiting for what they had been promised of punishment. The first is preferable.

﴿So they were not able to rise up﴾: that is, they were not able to stand.

Qatada said: "to rise" means they did not get up from that fall. The meaning is that they were unable to stand, let alone flee. Similar to it is His saying: ﴿So they became in their homes prostrate﴾ [al-A'raf: 78].

﴿Nor were they able to defend themselves﴾: that is, they could not protect themselves from God's punishment by means of others.

﴿And the people of Nuh before, [for] indeed they were a people who were defiantly disobedient﴾: that is, before these destroyed ones, for their time preceded the time of Fir'awn, 'Ad and Thamud. ﴿Indeed they were a people who were defiantly disobedient﴾: that is, they were outside the obedience of God.

Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Abu 'Amr read qawmin in the genitive (khafd), that is: and in the people of Nuh is a sign. The rest read it in the accusative, that is: and We destroyed the people of Nuh; or it is conjoined to the object of "the thunderbolt seized them," or to the object of "We cast them," that is: We cast them and We cast the people of Nuh; or the governing element of it may be "remember" (udhkur).

﴿And the heaven We built with power﴾: that is, with strength and capability. The majority read al-sama' in the accusative, by the construction of preoccupation (al-ishtighal, where the verb is occupied with a pronoun of the noun), and the presumed meaning is: "and We built the heaven, We built it." Abu al-Simak and Ibn Miqsam read it in the nominative, by the construction of the beginning (al-ibtida').

﴿And indeed We are expanding﴾: al-muwassi'un is one who possesses expanse and ampleness. The meaning is: indeed We are possessors of expanse in creating it and creating other than it; We are not incapable of that. It was said: "We are capable," from al-wus' in the sense of ability and power. It was said: "Indeed We are expanding provision by rain." Al-Jawhari said: and awsa'a al-rajul means: he became one of ampleness and wealth.

﴿And the earth, We spread it out﴾: the majority read al-ard in the accusative by the construction of preoccupation, and Abu al-Simak and Ibn Miqsam read it in the nominative as previously mentioned in His saying: ﴿And the heaven, We built it﴾. The meaning of "We spread it out" is: We spread it like a bed. ﴿So how excellent are the spreaders﴾: that is, we are. One says: mahadtu al-firash, I spread the bed and made it level; and tamhid al-umur is arranging and setting them right.

﴿And of everything We created pairs﴾: that is, two kinds and two types of male and female, land and sea, sun and moon, sweet and bitter, sky and earth, night and day, light and darkness, jinn and humans, good and evil, ﴿that perhaps you might remember﴾: that is, We created that in this way so that you would remember, and know that He is the Creator of everything, and derive evidence from that for His oneness and the truth of His promise and His threat.

﴿So flee to God; indeed I am a clear warner to you from Him﴾: that is, say to them, O Muhammad: "So flee to God by repentance from your sins, from disbelief and disobedience." The clause ﴿indeed I am a clear warner to you from Him﴾ is a justification for the command to flee. It was said the meaning of ﴿so flee to God﴾ is: leave Makkah.

al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: be wary of everything other than God, for whoever flees to other than Him will not be protected from Him.

It was said: flee from the obedience of Satan to the obedience of the Merciful; it was said: flee from ignorance to knowledge.

The meaning of ﴿indeed I am to you from Him﴾: that is, from His side I am a warner, clear in warning.

﴿And do not make with God another god﴾: He forbade them from associating partners with God after commanding them to flee to God.

The clause ﴿indeed I am to you from Him a clear warner﴾ is a justification for the prohibition.

﴿Thus did no messenger come to those before them but they said: a sorcerer or a madman.﴾ In this is consolation for the Messenger of God (ﷺ), by clarifying that this is the way of the earlier nations, and that what occurred from the Arabs in denying the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and describing him with sorcery and madness had also occurred from those before them toward their messengers. Likewise (kadhalika) is in the place of a nominative, as the predicate of an omitted subject: that is, the matter is thus.

Then He explained what He had summarized with His saying: "what came..." etc. Or it is in the place of an accusative as a qualifier of an omitted verbal noun: that is, "I warn you with a warning like the warning of those messengers before me who warned their peoples." The first is preferable.

﴿Did they bequeath it to one another?﴾ The interrogation is for reproach, rebuke and wonder at their condition: that is, did the first of them enjoin on the last of them denial, and agree together upon it?

﴿Rather they are a people who are transgressors﴾: a retraction (idrab) from the notion of mutual bequeathing to what gathered them, which is transgression. That is: they did not bequeath it to one another; rather transgression gathered them, and it is exceeding the limit in disbelief.

Then God, glorified is He, commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to turn away from them, saying: ﴿So turn away from them﴾: that is, turn away from them, cease disputing with them and calling them to the truth, for you have done what God commanded you and conveyed His message. ﴿And you are not blameworthy﴾ before God after this, because you have fulfilled what is upon you. This is abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of the sword (ayat al-sayf).

Then, when He commanded him to turn away from them, He commanded him not to cease reminding and admonishing with what is best, saying: ﴿And remind, for indeed the reminder benefits the believers.﴾ Al-Kalbi said: the meaning is: admonish with the Qur'an whoever among your people has believed, for the reminder benefits them.

Muqatil said: admonish the disbelievers of Makkah, for the reminder benefits whoever, in God's knowledge, will believe.

It was said: remind them of the punishment and the Days of God. He specified the believers for reminding because they are the ones who benefit from it.

The clause ﴿And I did not create the jinn and humankind except to worship Me﴾ is a resumed clause confirming what precedes it, because the fact that their creation was for the mere purpose of worship is something that energizes the Messenger of God (ﷺ) for reminding, and energizes them to respond.

It was said: this is specific to those who, in God's knowledge, will worship Him; it is a general statement intended in a specific sense.

Al-Wahidi said: the exegetes said: this is specific to the people of His obedience, meaning those among both groups who are qualified.

He said: this is the saying of al-Kalbi, al-Dahhak, and the preference of al-Farra' and Ibn Qutayba.

Al-Qushayri said: the verse has definitely entered into specification, because the insane were not commanded to worship, nor did He intend it from them, and He has said: ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and humankind﴾ [al-A'raf: 179], and whoever is created for Hell is not among those created for worship.

So the verse is to be understood as referring to the believers among them, and this is indicated by the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "And I did not create the jinn and humankind among the believers except to worship Me."

Mujahid said: the meaning is: except that they may know Me.

Al-Tha'labi said: this is a fine saying, because if He had not created them, His existence and oneness would not have been known.

It is narrated from Mujahid that he said: the meaning is: except that I might command them and forbid them. This is indicated by His saying: ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship one God; there is no deity but Him; exalted is He above what they associate﴾ [al-Tawba: 31]. al-Zajjaj preferred this.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: it is what they were disposed to of happiness and wretchedness; so He created the happy among the jinn and humankind for worship, and created the wretched for disobedience.

Al-Kalbi said: the meaning is: except that they may declare Me one; as for the believer, he declares Him one in hardship and ease; as for the disbeliever, he declares Him one in hardship but not in blessing, as in His saying: ﴿And when a wave covers them like shadows, they call upon God, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Luqman: 32]. 

A group said: except that they may submit to Me and humble themselves. The meaning of worship in the language is: humiliation, submission and compliance. Every created being of humankind and jinn is subject to God's decree, humbled to His will, and compliant with what He has determined for him.

He created them as He willed, and provided for them as He decreed. None of them possesses for himself any benefit or harm.

The reason for mentioning the jinn before humankind here is the precedence of their existence.

﴿I do not want from them any provision, nor do I want them to feed Me.﴾ This sentence contains a clarification of His, glorified is He, independence from His servants, and that He does not want from them any benefit, as masters want from their slaves; rather He is the absolutely Rich, the Provider, the Giver.

It was said the meaning is: I do not want from them that they provide for anyone of My creation, nor that they provide for themselves, nor that they feed anyone of My creation nor feed themselves. He attributed feeding to Himself because all creation are God's dependents; whoever feeds God's dependents is as if he fed Him.

This is like what came in the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "God says: My servant, I asked you for food and you did not feed Me." That is, you did not feed My servants. And "min" in His saying "min rizq" (of provision) is extra, for the emphasis of generality.

﴿When We sent him to Fir'awn with a manifest authority.﴾ The adverbial phrase (al-zarf) is connected to an omitted element which is the qualifier (na't) of the sign: that is, existing at the time We sent him; or it is connected to the sign itself. The first is preferable.

The manifest authority (al-sultan al-mubin) is the clear, evident proof, and it is the staff and what accompanied it of signs.

﴿But he turned away with his rukn.﴾ Al-tawalli is turning away (al-i'rad), and al-rukn is the side. This was said by al-Akhfash.

The meaning is: he turned away with his side, as in His saying: ﴿He turned away and withdrew with his side﴾ [al-Isra': 83]. Al-Jawhari said: the rukn of a thing is its strongest side, and "he takes refuge in a firm rukn" means: in might and protection.

Ibn Zayd, Mujahid and others said: the rukn is his army and his soldiers by whom he strengthened himself. From it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or I would take refuge in a firm rukn﴾ [Hud: 80], that is: a clan and protection. It was also said: the rukn is strength itself, and Qatada and others said this. From it is the saying of 'Antara:

"The rigors of war have not weakened my rukn,
but rather what has passed of my time."

﴿And he said: a sorcerer or a madman.﴾ That is, Fir'awn said concerning Musa: "He is a sorcerer or a madman." He vacillated, in regard to what he saw of Musa's conditions, between his being a sorcerer or a madman. This from the accursed one is a sophistry and a deception to his people, for he knows that what he saw of the marvels cannot be easily accomplished at the hand of a sorcerer, nor does one who is mad do such things.

It was said: "or" (aw) here has the meaning of "and" (wa), because he said all of that together and did not vacillate. This was said by al-Mu'arrij and al-Farra', like His saying: ﴿And do not obey from among them a sinner or a disbeliever﴾ [al-Insan: 24].

﴿So We seized him and his soldiers, and We cast them into the sea.﴾ That is, We threw them into the sea. The clause ﴿and he was blameworthy﴾ is in the place of an accusative as a circumstantial state (hal): that is, one who came with what he deserves to be blamed for, when he claimed lordship, disbelieved in God, and transgressed in his disobedience.

﴿And in 'Ad﴾: that is, and We left in the story of 'Ad a sign ﴿when We sent upon them the barren wind﴾, which is the one in which there is no good nor blessing, which does not fertilize trees nor bring rain; it is only a wind of destruction and punishment.

Then He, glorified is He, described this wind, saying: ﴿It left nothing it passed over but made it like the crumbled﴾. That is: it left nothing that passed over them, of their persons, their livestock and their wealth, but made it like a thing destroyed and decayed.

The poet said:

"Time left me when it withdrew from my sight,
and I remained like the decayed bone of the rimma."

Qatada said: it is what is trampled of dry vegetation. Al-Suddi and Abu al-'Aliya said: it is pulverized dust. Qutrub said: it is ash. The root of the word is from "ramma al-'azm": when a bone decays, it becomes rameem (crumbled). And al-rimma is decayed bones.

﴿And in Thamud, when it was said to them: enjoy yourselves until a time.﴾ That is, and We left in the story of Thamud a sign at the time We said to them: live enjoying the world until the time of destruction, which was three days, as in His saying: ﴿Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days﴾ [Hud: 65].

﴿But they defied the command of their Lord﴾: that is, they became arrogant regarding obedience to God's command. ﴿So the thunderbolt seized them﴾, and it is every destroying punishment.

The majority read al-sa'iqa (the thunderbolt). 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, Humayd, Ibn Muhaysin, Mujahid and al-Kisa'i read al-sa'qa. The discussion of al-sa'iqa has passed in al-Baqara and in other places. ﴿While they were looking﴾: that is, they were seeing it with their own eyes. The clause is in the place of an accusative as a circumstantial state. It was said that the meaning is: they were waiting for what they had been promised of punishment. The first is preferable.

﴿So they were not able to rise up﴾: that is, they were not able to stand.

Qatada said: "to rise" means they did not get up from that fall. The meaning is that they were unable to stand, let alone flee. Similar to it is His saying: ﴿So they became in their homes prostrate﴾ [al-A'raf: 78].

﴿Nor were they able to defend themselves﴾: that is, they could not protect themselves from God's punishment by means of others.

﴿And the people of Nuh before, [for] indeed they were a people who were defiantly disobedient﴾: that is, before these destroyed ones, for their time preceded the time of Fir'awn, 'Ad and Thamud. ﴿Indeed they were a people who were defiantly disobedient﴾: that is, they were outside the obedience of God.

Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Abu 'Amr read qawmin in the genitive (khafd), that is: and in the people of Nuh is a sign. The rest read it in the accusative, that is: and We destroyed the people of Nuh; or it is conjoined to the object of "the thunderbolt seized them," or to the object of "We cast them," that is: We cast them and We cast the people of Nuh; or the governing element of it may be "remember" (udhkur).

﴿And the heaven We built with power﴾: that is, with strength and capability. The majority read al-sama' in the accusative, by the construction of preoccupation (al-ishtighal, where the verb is occupied with a pronoun of the noun), and the presumed meaning is: "and We built the heaven, We built it." Abu al-Simak and Ibn Miqsam read it in the nominative, by the construction of the beginning (al-ibtida').

﴿And indeed We are expanding﴾: al-muwassi'un is one who possesses expanse and ampleness. The meaning is: indeed We are possessors of expanse in creating it and creating other than it; We are not incapable of that. It was said: "We are capable," from al-wus' in the sense of ability and power. It was said: "Indeed We are expanding provision by rain." Al-Jawhari said: and awsa'a al-rajul means: he became one of ampleness and wealth.

﴿And the earth, We spread it out﴾: the majority read al-ard in the accusative by the construction of preoccupation, and Abu al-Simak and Ibn Miqsam read it in the nominative as previously mentioned in His saying: ﴿And the heaven, We built it﴾. The meaning of "We spread it out" is: We spread it like a bed. ﴿So how excellent are the spreaders﴾: that is, we are. One says: mahadtu al-firash, I spread the bed and made it level; and tamhid al-umur is arranging and setting them right.

﴿And of everything We created pairs﴾: that is, two kinds and two types of male and female, land and sea, sun and moon, sweet and bitter, sky and earth, night and day, light and darkness, jinn and humans, good and evil, ﴿that perhaps you might remember﴾: that is, We created that in this way so that you would remember, and know that He is the Creator of everything, and derive evidence from that for His oneness and the truth of His promise and His threat.

﴿So flee to God; indeed I am a clear warner to you from Him﴾: that is, say to them, O Muhammad: "So flee to God by repentance from your sins, from disbelief and disobedience." The clause ﴿indeed I am a clear warner to you from Him﴾ is a justification for the command to flee. It was said the meaning of ﴿so flee to God﴾ is: leave Makkah.

al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: be wary of everything other than God, for whoever flees to other than Him will not be protected from Him.

It was said: flee from the obedience of Satan to the obedience of the Merciful; it was said: flee from ignorance to knowledge.

The meaning of ﴿indeed I am to you from Him﴾: that is, from His side I am a warner, clear in warning.

﴿And do not make with God another god﴾: He forbade them from associating partners with God after commanding them to flee to God.

The clause ﴿indeed I am to you from Him a clear warner﴾ is a justification for the prohibition.

﴿Thus did no messenger come to those before them but they said: a sorcerer or a madman.﴾ In this is consolation for the Messenger of God (ﷺ), by clarifying that this is the way of the earlier nations, and that what occurred from the Arabs in denying the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and describing him with sorcery and madness had also occurred from those before them toward their messengers. Likewise (kadhalika) is in the place of a nominative, as the predicate of an omitted subject: that is, the matter is thus.

Then He explained what He had summarized with His saying: "what came..." etc. Or it is in the place of an accusative as a qualifier of an omitted verbal noun: that is, "I warn you with a warning like the warning of those messengers before me who warned their peoples." The first is preferable.

﴿Did they bequeath it to one another?﴾ The interrogation is for reproach, rebuke and wonder at their condition: that is, did the first of them enjoin on the last of them denial, and agree together upon it?

﴿Rather they are a people who are transgressors﴾: a retraction (idrab) from the notion of mutual bequeathing to what gathered them, which is transgression. That is: they did not bequeath it to one another; rather transgression gathered them, and it is exceeding the limit in disbelief.

Then God, glorified is He, commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to turn away from them, saying: ﴿So turn away from them﴾: that is, turn away from them, cease disputing with them and calling them to the truth, for you have done what God commanded you and conveyed His message. ﴿And you are not blameworthy﴾ before God after this, because you have fulfilled what is upon you. This is abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of the sword (ayat al-sayf).

Then, when He commanded him to turn away from them, He commanded him not to cease reminding and admonishing with what is best, saying: ﴿And remind, for indeed the reminder benefits the believers.﴾ Al-Kalbi said: the meaning is: admonish with the Qur'an whoever among your people has believed, for the reminder benefits them.

Muqatil said: admonish the disbelievers of Makkah, for the reminder benefits whoever, in God's knowledge, will believe.

It was said: remind them of the punishment and the Days of God. He specified the believers for reminding because they are the ones who benefit from it.

The clause ﴿And I did not create the jinn and humankind except to worship Me﴾ is a resumed clause confirming what precedes it, because the fact that their creation was for the mere purpose of worship is something that energizes the Messenger of God (ﷺ) for reminding, and energizes them to respond.

It was said: this is specific to those who, in God's knowledge, will worship Him; it is a general statement intended in a specific sense.

Al-Wahidi said: the exegetes said: this is specific to the people of His obedience, meaning those among both groups who are qualified.

He said: this is the saying of al-Kalbi, al-Dahhak, and the preference of al-Farra' and Ibn Qutayba.

Al-Qushayri said: the verse has definitely entered into specification, because the insane were not commanded to worship, nor did He intend it from them, and He has said: ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and humankind﴾ [al-A'raf: 179], and whoever is created for Hell is not among those created for worship.

So the verse is to be understood as referring to the believers among them, and this is indicated by the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "And I did not create the jinn and humankind among the believers except to worship Me."

Mujahid said: the meaning is: except that they may know Me.

Al-Tha'labi said: this is a fine saying, because if He had not created them, His existence and oneness would not have been known.

It is narrated from Mujahid that he said: the meaning is: except that I might command them and forbid them. This is indicated by His saying: ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship one God; there is no deity but Him; exalted is He above what they associate﴾ [al-Tawba: 31]. al-Zajjaj preferred this.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: it is what they were disposed to of happiness and wretchedness; so He created the happy among the jinn and humankind for worship, and created the wretched for disobedience.

Al-Kalbi said: the meaning is: except that they may declare Me one; as for the believer, he declares Him one in hardship and ease; as for the disbeliever, he declares Him one in hardship but not in blessing, as in His saying: ﴿And when a wave covers them like shadows, they call upon God, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Luqman: 32]. 

A group said: except that they may submit to Me and humble themselves. The meaning of worship in the language is: humiliation, submission and compliance. Every created being of humankind and jinn is subject to God's decree, humbled to His will, and compliant with what He has determined for him.

He created them as He willed, and provided for them as He decreed. None of them possesses for himself any benefit or harm.

The reason for mentioning the jinn before humankind here is the precedence of their existence.

﴿I do not want from them any provision, nor do I want them to feed Me.﴾ This sentence contains a clarification of His, glorified is He, independence from His servants, and that He does not want from them any benefit, as masters want from their slaves; rather He is the absolutely Rich, the Provider, the Giver.

It was said the meaning is: I do not want from them that they provide for anyone of My creation, nor that they provide for themselves, nor that they feed anyone of My creation nor feed themselves. He attributed feeding to Himself because all creation are God's dependents; whoever feeds God's dependents is as if he fed Him.

This is like what came in the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "God says: My servant, I asked you for food and you did not feed Me." That is, you did not feed My servants. And "min" in His saying "min rizq" (of provision) is extra, for the emphasis of generality.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 51, verse 38–60 (part 2 of 2):

Then the Exalted showed that He alone is the Provider (al-Razzaq), and none other. He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Provider, Possessor of power, the Firm.﴾ There is no provider besides Him and no giver other than Him. He is the One who provides for His creatures and takes care of what sustains them, so that they should not busy themselves with other than that for which they were created, namely worship. ﴿Possessor of power, the Firm﴾: the nominative (al-raf') of al-matin (the Firm) may be as an attribute of al-Razzaq, or of "dhu" (Possessor), or as the predicate of an omitted subject, or as a second predicate.

The majority of readers recite al-Razzaq. Ibn Muhaysin read al-Raziq. The majority read al-matin in the nominative. Yahya ibn Wathhab and al-A'mash read it in the genitive (al-jarr), as an attribute of al-quwwah (power). The masculine form is used because its feminine is not a true feminine.

Al-Farra' said: its correct form would have been al-matinah (feminine), but he made it masculine because he had in mind "the thing that is firm, well-twisted." One says a rope is matin, meaning well-twisted. The meaning of al-matin here is: intensely strong.

﴿Indeed, for those who have done wrong is a share (dhanub) like the share of their companions﴾: that is, they wronged themselves by disbelief and sins, so for them is a share (dhanub), i.e., a portion of punishment, like the portion of the disbelievers of the previous nations. Ibn al-A'rabi said: one says "a day of dhanub," meaning a day of long evil that does not end. The original meaning of dhanub in the language is a large bucket. Among the uses of dhanub for a portion of something is the poet's saying:

"By your life, and the fates are coming upon all the sons of one father, each has a dhanub of them."

What is in the verse is taken from the sharing of water-carriers by the large bucket, so it is a metaphor, in which dhanub is put in place of share and portion, as Ibn Qutaybah said. ﴿So let them not seek to hasten Me﴾: that is, let them not ask Me to hasten the punishment for them, as in their saying: ﴿Bring us what you promise us, if you are among the truthful.﴾

﴿So woe to those who disbelieved from their day which they are promised.﴾ It has been said that it is the Day of Resurrection, and it has been said that it is the Day of Badr. The fa' (so) indicates the sequence of what follows upon what precedes.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted, regarding His saying ﴿but he turned away with his pillar﴾, from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "with his people."

al-Firyabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, transmitted from him regarding His saying ﴿the barren wind﴾ that he said: "the violent one which does not fertilize anything."

Ibn Jarir also transmitted from him, that he said: "it does not fertilize trees nor stir up clouds." And regarding His saying ﴿but it left it like rotted debris﴾ he said: "like a thing that has perished."

al-Firyabi and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib that he said: "The barren wind is the nakba'" (a wind blowing from an unusual direction).

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying ﴿And the heaven We built with hands﴾ that he said: "with power."

Abu Dawud in his al-Nasikh and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from him regarding His saying ﴿So turn away from them, for you are not blameworthy﴾ that he said: "Allah commanded him to turn away from them in order to punish them, and excused Muhammad (ﷺ). Then He said: ﴿And remind, for the reminder benefits the believers﴾, and this abrogated it."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from him regarding His saying ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾ that he said: "to acknowledge servitude, willingly or unwillingly."

Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from him regarding the verse, that he said: "upon what I created them upon of obedience to Me and disobedience, of misery and happiness."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat transmitted from him also regarding His saying: "al-Matin" says: "the strong."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from him also regarding His saying: "dhanuban" he said: "a bucket."

His saying: "And in Musa" is conjoined to his saying "in it" (fihā) with the repetition of the preposition, and the implied meaning is: "And We left in the story of Musa a sign." Or it is conjoined to "and in the earth," and the implied meaning is: "And in the earth and in Musa are signs." This is what al-Farra', Ibn 'Atiyya and al-Zamakhshari said.

Abu Hayyan said: "This is very far-fetched; the Qur'an is too exalted for the like of it." It is also permissible that it be connected to a presumed "We made" (ja'alna), which is indicated by "We left" (taraknā). It was said: it is also permissible that it be conjoined to "We left" in the manner of the saying of the poet:

"I fed them chaff and cold water,"

and the implied meaning is: "We left in it a sign, and We placed in Musa a sign."

Likewise (kadhalika) is in the place of a nominative, as the predicate of an omitted subject: that is, the matter is thus.

Then He explained what He had summarized with His saying: "what came..." etc. Or it is in the place of an accusative as a qualifier of an omitted verbal noun: that is, "I warn you with a warning like the warning of those messengers before me who warned their peoples." The first is preferable.

﴿Did they bequeath it to one another?﴾ The interrogation is for reproach, rebuke and wonder at their condition: that is, did the first of them enjoin on the last of them denial, and agree together upon it?

﴿Rather they are a people who are transgressors﴾: a retraction (idrab) from the notion of mutual bequeathing to what gathered them, which is transgression. That is: they did not bequeath it to one another; rather transgression gathered them, and it is exceeding the limit in disbelief.

Then God, glorified is He, commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to turn away from them, saying: ﴿So turn away from them﴾: that is, turn away from them, cease disputing with them and calling them to the truth, for you have done what God commanded you and conveyed His message. ﴿And you are not blameworthy﴾ before God after this, because you have fulfilled what is upon you. This is abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of the sword (ayat al-sayf).

Then, when He commanded him to turn away from them, He commanded him not to cease reminding and admonishing with what is best, saying: ﴿And remind, for indeed the reminder benefits the believers.﴾ Al-Kalbi said: the meaning is: admonish with the Qur'an whoever among your people has believed, for the reminder benefits them.

Muqatil said: admonish the disbelievers of Makkah, for the reminder benefits whoever, in God's knowledge, will believe.

It was said: remind them of the punishment and the Days of God. He specified the believers for reminding because they are the ones who benefit from it.

The clause ﴿And I did not create the jinn and humankind except to worship Me﴾ is a resumed clause confirming what precedes it, because the fact that their creation was for the mere purpose of worship is something that energizes the Messenger of God (ﷺ) for reminding, and energizes them to respond.

It was said: this is specific to those who, in God's knowledge, will worship Him; it is a general statement intended in a specific sense.

Al-Wahidi said: the exegetes said: this is specific to the people of His obedience, meaning those among both groups who are qualified.

He said: this is the saying of al-Kalbi, al-Dahhak, and the preference of al-Farra' and Ibn Qutayba.

Al-Qushayri said: the verse has definitely entered into specification, because the insane were not commanded to worship, nor did He intend it from them, and He has said: ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and humankind﴾ [al-A'raf: 179], and whoever is created for Hell is not among those created for worship.

So the verse is to be understood as referring to the believers among them, and this is indicated by the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "And I did not create the jinn and humankind among the believers except to worship Me."

Mujahid said: the meaning is: except that they may know Me.

Al-Tha'labi said: this is a fine saying, because if He had not created them, His existence and oneness would not have been known.

It is narrated from Mujahid that he said: the meaning is: except that I might command them and forbid them. This is indicated by His saying: ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship one God; there is no deity but Him; exalted is He above what they associate﴾ [al-Tawba: 31]. al-Zajjaj preferred this.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: it is what they were disposed to of happiness and wretchedness; so He created the happy among the jinn and humankind for worship, and created the wretched for disobedience.

Al-Kalbi said: the meaning is: except that they may declare Me one; as for the believer, he declares Him one in hardship and ease; as for the disbeliever, he declares Him one in hardship but not in blessing, as in His saying: ﴿And when a wave covers them like shadows, they call upon God, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Luqman: 32]. 

A group said: except that they may submit to Me and humble themselves. The meaning of worship in the language is: humiliation, submission and compliance. Every created being of humankind and jinn is subject to God's decree, humbled to His will, and compliant with what He has determined for him.

He created them as He willed, and provided for them as He decreed. None of them possesses for himself any benefit or harm.

The reason for mentioning the jinn before humankind here is the precedence of their existence.

﴿I do not want from them any provision, nor do I want them to feed Me.﴾ This sentence contains a clarification of His, glorified is He, independence from His servants, and that He does not want from them any benefit, as masters want from their slaves; rather He is the absolutely Rich, the Provider, the Giver.

It was said the meaning is: I do not want from them that they provide for anyone of My creation, nor that they provide for themselves, nor that they feed anyone of My creation nor feed themselves. He attributed feeding to Himself because all creation are God's dependents; whoever feeds God's dependents is as if he fed Him.

This is like what came in the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "God says: My servant, I asked you for food and you did not feed Me." That is, you did not feed My servants. And "min" in His saying "min rizq" (of provision) is extra, for the emphasis of generality.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 51, verse 38–60 (part 2 of 2):

Then the Exalted showed that He alone is the Provider (al-Razzaq), and none other. He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Provider, Possessor of power, the Firm.﴾ There is no provider besides Him and no giver other than Him. He is the One who provides for His creatures and takes care of what sustains them, so that they should not busy themselves with other than that for which they were created, namely worship. ﴿Possessor of power, the Firm﴾: the nominative (al-raf') of al-matin (the Firm) may be as an attribute of al-Razzaq, or of "dhu" (Possessor), or as the predicate of an omitted subject, or as a second predicate.

The majority of readers recite al-Razzaq. Ibn Muhaysin read al-Raziq. The majority read al-matin in the nominative. Yahya ibn Wathhab and al-A'mash read it in the genitive (al-jarr), as an attribute of al-quwwah (power). The masculine form is used because its feminine is not a true feminine.

Al-Farra' said: its correct form would have been al-matinah (feminine), but he made it masculine because he had in mind "the thing that is firm, well-twisted." One says a rope is matin, meaning well-twisted. The meaning of al-matin here is: intensely strong.

﴿Indeed, for those who have done wrong is a share (dhanub) like the share of their companions﴾: that is, they wronged themselves by disbelief and sins, so for them is a share (dhanub), i.e., a portion of punishment, like the portion of the disbelievers of the previous nations. Ibn al-A'rabi said: one says "a day of dhanub," meaning a day of long evil that does not end. The original meaning of dhanub in the language is a large bucket. Among the uses of dhanub for a portion of something is the poet's saying:

"By your life, and the fates are coming upon all the sons of one father, each has a dhanub of them."

What is in the verse is taken from the sharing of water-carriers by the large bucket, so it is a metaphor, in which dhanub is put in place of share and portion, as Ibn Qutaybah said. ﴿So let them not seek to hasten Me﴾: that is, let them not ask Me to hasten the punishment for them, as in their saying: ﴿Bring us what you promise us, if you are among the truthful.﴾

﴿So woe to those who disbelieved from their day which they are promised.﴾ It has been said that it is the Day of Resurrection, and it has been said that it is the Day of Badr. The fa' (so) indicates the sequence of what follows upon what precedes.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted, regarding His saying ﴿but he turned away with his pillar﴾, from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "with his people."

al-Firyabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, transmitted from him regarding His saying ﴿the barren wind﴾ that he said: "the violent one which does not fertilize anything."

Ibn Jarir also transmitted from him, that he said: "it does not fertilize trees nor stir up clouds." And regarding His saying ﴿but it left it like rotted debris﴾ he said: "like a thing that has perished."

al-Firyabi and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib that he said: "The barren wind is the nakba'" (a wind blowing from an unusual direction).

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying ﴿And the heaven We built with hands﴾ that he said: "with power."

Abu Dawud in his al-Nasikh and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from him regarding His saying ﴿So turn away from them, for you are not blameworthy﴾ that he said: "Allah commanded him to turn away from them in order to punish them, and excused Muhammad (ﷺ). Then He said: ﴿And remind, for the reminder benefits the believers﴾, and this abrogated it."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from him regarding His saying ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾ that he said: "to acknowledge servitude, willingly or unwillingly."

Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from him regarding the verse, that he said: "upon what I created them upon of obedience to Me and disobedience, of misery and happiness."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat transmitted from him also regarding His saying: "al-Matin" says: "the strong."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from him also regarding His saying: "dhanuban" he said: "a bucket."

His saying: "And in Musa" is conjoined to his saying "in it" (fihā) with the repetition of the preposition, and the implied meaning is: "And We left in the story of Musa a sign." Or it is conjoined to "and in the earth," and the implied meaning is: "And in the earth and in Musa are signs." This is what al-Farra', Ibn 'Atiyya and al-Zamakhshari said.

Abu Hayyan said: "This is very far-fetched; the Qur'an is too exalted for the like of it." It is also permissible that it be connected to a presumed "We made" (ja'alna), which is indicated by "We left" (taraknā). It was said: it is also permissible that it be conjoined to "We left" in the manner of the saying of the poet:

"I fed them chaff and cold water,"

and the implied meaning is: "We left in it a sign, and We placed in Musa a sign."

Abu Hayyan said: "There is no need to presume 'We placed,' because it is possible that the governing element of the genitive (majrur) is 'We left.'"

The first mode is the preferable one, and whatever else there is, is forced and strained; no need compels to it, and no necessity calls for it.

﴿When We sent him to Fir'awn with a manifest authority.﴾ The adverbial phrase (al-zarf) is connected to an omitted element which is the qualifier (na't) of the sign: that is, existing at the time We sent him; or it is connected to the sign itself. The first is preferable.

The manifest authority (al-sultan al-mubin) is the clear, evident proof, and it is the staff and what accompanied it of signs.

﴿But he turned away with his rukn.﴾ Al-tawalli is turning away (al-i'rad), and al-rukn is the side. This was said by al-Akhfash.

The meaning is: he turned away with his side, as in His saying: ﴿He turned away and withdrew with his side﴾ [al-Isra': 83]. Al-Jawhari said: the rukn of a thing is its strongest side, and "he takes refuge in a firm rukn" means: in might and protection.

Ibn Zayd, Mujahid and others said: the rukn is his army and his soldiers by whom he strengthened himself. From it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or I would take refuge in a firm rukn﴾ [Hud: 80], that is: a clan and protection. It was also said: the rukn is strength itself, and Qatada and others said this. From it is the saying of 'Antara:

"The rigors of war have not weakened my rukn,
but rather what has passed of my time."

﴿And he said: a sorcerer or a madman.﴾ That is, Fir'awn said concerning Musa: "He is a sorcerer or a madman." He vacillated, in regard to what he saw of Musa's conditions, between his being a sorcerer or a madman. This from the accursed one is a sophistry and a deception to his people, for he knows that what he saw of the marvels cannot be easily accomplished at the hand of a sorcerer, nor does one who is mad do such things.

It was said: "or" (aw) here has the meaning of "and" (wa), because he said all of that together and did not vacillate. This was said by al-Mu'arrij and al-Farra', like His saying: ﴿And do not obey from among them a sinner or a disbeliever﴾ [al-Insan: 24].

﴿So We seized him and his soldiers, and We cast them into the sea.﴾ That is, We threw them into the sea. The clause ﴿and he was blameworthy﴾ is in the place of an accusative as a circumstantial state (hal): that is, one who came with what he deserves to be blamed for, when he claimed lordship, disbelieved in God, and transgressed in his disobedience.

﴿And in 'Ad﴾: that is, and We left in the story of 'Ad a sign ﴿when We sent upon them the barren wind﴾, which is the one in which there is no good nor blessing, which does not fertilize trees nor bring rain; it is only a wind of destruction and punishment.

Then He, glorified is He, described this wind, saying: ﴿It left nothing it passed over but made it like the crumbled﴾. That is: it left nothing that passed over them, of their persons, their livestock and their wealth, but made it like a thing destroyed and decayed.

The poet said:

"Time left me when it withdrew from my sight,
and I remained like the decayed bone of the rimma."

Qatada said: it is what is trampled of dry vegetation. Al-Suddi and Abu al-'Aliya said: it is pulverized dust. Qutrub said: it is ash. The root of the word is from "ramma al-'azm": when a bone decays, it becomes rameem (crumbled). And al-rimma is decayed bones.

﴿And in Thamud, when it was said to them: enjoy yourselves until a time.﴾ That is, and We left in the story of Thamud a sign at the time We said to them: live enjoying the world until the time of destruction, which was three days, as in His saying: ﴿Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days﴾ [Hud: 65].

﴿But they defied the command of their Lord﴾: that is, they became arrogant regarding obedience to God's command. ﴿So the thunderbolt seized them﴾, and it is every destroying punishment.

The majority read al-sa'iqa (the thunderbolt). 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, Humayd, Ibn Muhaysin, Mujahid and al-Kisa'i read al-sa'qa. The discussion of al-sa'iqa has passed in al-Baqara and in other places. ﴿While they were looking﴾: that is, they were seeing it with their own eyes. The clause is in the place of an accusative as a circumstantial state. It was said that the meaning is: they were waiting for what they had been promised of punishment. The first is preferable.

﴿So they were not able to rise up﴾: that is, they were not able to stand.

Qatada said: "to rise" means they did not get up from that fall. The meaning is that they were unable to stand, let alone flee. Similar to it is His saying: ﴿So they became in their homes prostrate﴾ [al-A'raf: 78].

﴿Nor were they able to defend themselves﴾: that is, they could not protect themselves from God's punishment by means of others.

﴿And the people of Nuh before, [for] indeed they were a people who were defiantly disobedient﴾: that is, before these destroyed ones, for their time preceded the time of Fir'awn, 'Ad and Thamud. ﴿Indeed they were a people who were defiantly disobedient﴾: that is, they were outside the obedience of God.

Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Abu 'Amr read qawmin in the genitive (khafd), that is: and in the people of Nuh is a sign. The rest read it in the accusative, that is: and We destroyed the people of Nuh; or it is conjoined to the object of "the thunderbolt seized them," or to the object of "We cast them," that is: We cast them and We cast the people of Nuh; or the governing element of it may be "remember" (udhkur).

﴿And the heaven We built with power﴾: that is, with strength and capability. The majority read al-sama' in the accusative, by the construction of preoccupation (al-ishtighal, where the verb is occupied with a pronoun of the noun), and the presumed meaning is: "and We built the heaven, We built it." Abu al-Simak and Ibn Miqsam read it in the nominative, by the construction of the beginning (al-ibtida').

﴿And indeed We are expanding﴾: al-muwassi'un is one who possesses expanse and ampleness. The meaning is: indeed We are possessors of expanse in creating it and creating other than it; We are not incapable of that. It was said: "We are capable," from al-wus' in the sense of ability and power. It was said: "Indeed We are expanding provision by rain." Al-Jawhari said: and awsa'a al-rajul means: he became one of ampleness and wealth.

﴿And the earth, We spread it out﴾: the majority read al-ard in the accusative by the construction of preoccupation, and Abu al-Simak and Ibn Miqsam read it in the nominative as previously mentioned in His saying: ﴿And the heaven, We built it﴾. The meaning of "We spread it out" is: We spread it like a bed. ﴿So how excellent are the spreaders﴾: that is, we are. One says: mahadtu al-firash, I spread the bed and made it level; and tamhid al-umur is arranging and setting them right.

﴿And of everything We created pairs﴾: that is, two kinds and two types of male and female, land and sea, sun and moon, sweet and bitter, sky and earth, night and day, light and darkness, jinn and humans, good and evil, ﴿that perhaps you might remember﴾: that is, We created that in this way so that you would remember, and know that He is the Creator of everything, and derive evidence from that for His oneness and the truth of His promise and His threat.

﴿So flee to God; indeed I am a clear warner to you from Him﴾: that is, say to them, O Muhammad: "So flee to God by repentance from your sins, from disbelief and disobedience." The clause ﴿indeed I am a clear warner to you from Him﴾ is a justification for the command to flee. It was said the meaning of ﴿so flee to God﴾ is: leave Makkah.

al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: be wary of everything other than God, for whoever flees to other than Him will not be protected from Him.

It was said: flee from the obedience of Satan to the obedience of the Merciful; it was said: flee from ignorance to knowledge.

The meaning of ﴿indeed I am to you from Him﴾: that is, from His side I am a warner, clear in warning.

﴿And do not make with God another god﴾: He forbade them from associating partners with God after commanding them to flee to God.

The clause ﴿indeed I am to you from Him a clear warner﴾ is a justification for the prohibition.

﴿Thus did no messenger come to those before them but they said: a sorcerer or a madman.﴾ In this is consolation for the Messenger of God (ﷺ), by clarifying that this is the way of the earlier nations, and that what occurred from the Arabs in denying the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and describing him with sorcery and madness had also occurred from those before them toward their messengers. Likewise (kadhalika) is in the place of a nominative, as the predicate of an omitted subject: that is, the matter is thus.

Then He explained what He had summarized with His saying: "what came..." etc. Or it is in the place of an accusative as a qualifier of an omitted verbal noun: that is, "I warn you with a warning like the warning of those messengers before me who warned their peoples." The first is preferable.

﴿Did they bequeath it to one another?﴾ The interrogation is for reproach, rebuke and wonder at their condition: that is, did the first of them enjoin on the last of them denial, and agree together upon it?

﴿Rather they are a people who are transgressors﴾: a retraction (idrab) from the notion of mutual bequeathing to what gathered them, which is transgression. That is: they did not bequeath it to one another; rather transgression gathered them, and it is exceeding the limit in disbelief.

Then God, glorified is He, commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to turn away from them, saying: ﴿So turn away from them﴾: that is, turn away from them, cease disputing with them and calling them to the truth, for you have done what God commanded you and conveyed His message. ﴿And you are not blameworthy﴾ before God after this, because you have fulfilled what is upon you. This is abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of the sword (ayat al-sayf).

Then, when He commanded him to turn away from them, He commanded him not to cease reminding and admonishing with what is best, saying: ﴿And remind, for indeed the reminder benefits the believers.﴾ Al-Kalbi said: the meaning is: admonish with the Qur'an whoever among your people has believed, for the reminder benefits them.

Muqatil said: admonish the disbelievers of Makkah, for the reminder benefits whoever, in God's knowledge, will believe.

It was said: remind them of the punishment and the Days of God. He specified the believers for reminding because they are the ones who benefit from it.

The clause ﴿And I did not create the jinn and humankind except to worship Me﴾ is a resumed clause confirming what precedes it, because the fact that their creation was for the mere purpose of worship is something that energizes the Messenger of God (ﷺ) for reminding, and energizes them to respond.

It was said: this is specific to those who, in God's knowledge, will worship Him; it is a general statement intended in a specific sense.

Al-Wahidi said: the exegetes said: this is specific to the people of His obedience, meaning those among both groups who are qualified.

He said: this is the saying of al-Kalbi, al-Dahhak, and the preference of al-Farra' and Ibn Qutayba.

Al-Qushayri said: the verse has definitely entered into specification, because the insane were not commanded to worship, nor did He intend it from them, and He has said: ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and humankind﴾ [al-A'raf: 179], and whoever is created for Hell is not among those created for worship.

So the verse is to be understood as referring to the believers among them, and this is indicated by the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "And I did not create the jinn and humankind among the believers except to worship Me."

Mujahid said: the meaning is: except that they may know Me.

Al-Tha'labi said: this is a fine saying, because if He had not created them, His existence and oneness would not have been known.

It is narrated from Mujahid that he said: the meaning is: except that I might command them and forbid them. This is indicated by His saying: ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship one God; there is no deity but Him; exalted is He above what they associate﴾ [al-Tawba: 31]. al-Zajjaj preferred this.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: it is what they were disposed to of happiness and wretchedness; so He created the happy among the jinn and humankind for worship, and created the wretched for disobedience.

Al-Kalbi said: the meaning is: except that they may declare Me one; as for the believer, he declares Him one in hardship and ease; as for the disbeliever, he declares Him one in hardship but not in blessing, as in His saying: ﴿And when a wave covers them like shadows, they call upon God, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Luqman: 32]. 

A group said: except that they may submit to Me and humble themselves. The meaning of worship in the language is: humiliation, submission and compliance. Every created being of humankind and jinn is subject to God's decree, humbled to His will, and compliant with what He has determined for him.

He created them as He willed, and provided for them as He decreed. None of them possesses for himself any benefit or harm.

The reason for mentioning the jinn before humankind here is the precedence of their existence.

﴿I do not want from them any provision, nor do I want them to feed Me.﴾ This sentence contains a clarification of His, glorified is He, independence from His servants, and that He does not want from them any benefit, as masters want from their slaves; rather He is the absolutely Rich, the Provider, the Giver.

It was said the meaning is: I do not want from them that they provide for anyone of My creation, nor that they provide for themselves, nor that they feed anyone of My creation nor feed themselves. He attributed feeding to Himself because all creation are God's dependents; whoever feeds God's dependents is as if he fed Him.

This is like what came in the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "God says: My servant, I asked you for food and you did not feed Me." That is, you did not feed My servants. And "min" in His saying "min rizq" (of provision) is extra, for the emphasis of generality.
